content.text:
The scope is strong, but needs amendments before implementation: one recipe conflicts with Mosaic’s device ownership rules, and the ten-minute sample-integrity requirement exceeds the delivered capture API. Preserve the entire existing MIDI campaign, real-time-only Audio/Crow evidence, and automated acceptance without hardware or listening.

1. **Correct XA-004’s “same-player two channels” recipe.** Mosaic marks n.b. devices `unique = true` and excludes an assigned device from other channels’ selectors ([device_map.lua:353](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/devices/device_map.lua:353), [device_map.lua:521](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/devices/device_map.lua:521)). Test that exclusion, cancellation, and reassignment after freeing the device. Use distinct JF voice IDs for simultaneous channels. Do not bypass the picker or introduce shared-player support merely to satisfy this test.

2. **Make XA-020 achievable without expanding emulator scope unnecessarily.** Both captures permit eight jobs of at most 30 seconds: at most 240 captured seconds per session, with no guaranteed continuity between jobs ([audio-api.md:20](/mnt/c/Users/andy/Documents/ChatGPT/monome-emulator/docs/architecture/audio-api.md:20), [crow-capture-api.md:37](/mnt/c/Users/andy/Documents/ChatGPT/monome-emulator/docs/architecture/crow-capture-api.md:37)). Retain the ten-minute workload and complete MIDI/ii accounting, but specify bounded PCM/CV observation windows around selected transitions and final release; explicitly leave intervening samples unverified. If continuous ten-minute PCM/CV evidence is indispensable, identify a separate emulator capability dependency. Keep generic capture-limit, cursor and malformed-record conformance emulator-owned; Mosaic needs collector fault fixtures and a composed workflow guard.

3. **Add explicit n.b. parameter restoration and delayed-action ownership cases to XA-010.** This is a distinct backend seam: Mosaic saves a parameter’s original value, applies locks through global `params:set`, and restores it on a later trig ([step.lua:224](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/step.lua:224), [step.lua:245](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/step.lua:245)). Require lock→unlocked-trig restoration, including original zero; manual edit during a lock; and device/parameter reassignment while a slide remains queued. Assert the intended parameter and sound change, with no stale write to the previous target. Declare expected restoration semantics independently before running.

4. **Add live keyboard ownership explicitly, beyond recording/replay.** Keyboard audition has its own dispatch and release path, separate from sequenced playback ([m_midi.lua:109](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/m_midi.lua:109), [m_midi.lua:207](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/m_midi.lua:207)). Extend XA-013 with recording-disarmed audition, a held key across selected-channel/device changes, and a live note overlapping the same sequenced pitch. Observe the live output and final release as well as recorded playback. Existing broad recording language does not clearly guard this separate path.

5. **Make the JF inventory and shared-module constraints concrete.** XA-008 omits explicitly named unison, although the manual supports it and Mosaic allowlists it ([README.md:528](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/README.md:528), [device_map.lua:304](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/devices/device_map.lua:304)). Add unison, allocation exhaustion/stealing, and mode switching while notes/slew remain pending. The pinned player sends module-wide mode changes—kit uses mode 0, mono uses mode 1—and mono `stop_all` releases all voices ([nb_jf mod.lua:49](/mnt/c/Users/andy/Documents/ChatGPT/monome-emulator/.runtime/worktrees/audio-monitor/.runtime/nb-jf/source/lib/mod.lua:49), [mod.lua:126](/mnt/c/Users/andy/Documents/ChatGPT/monome-emulator/.runtime/worktrees/audio-monitor/.runtime/nb-jf/source/lib/mod.lua:126)). Distinct selector IDs therefore do not guarantee independent module ownership. Specify compatible combinations and conflict handling; do not demand simultaneous incompatible modes or infer downstream sound from packets.

6. **Strengthen oracle calibration with temporal negatives.** The scope already correctly rejects the old whole-recording frequency check and implementation-derived velocity formula ([mosaic_audio.py:42](/mnt/c/Users/andy/Documents/ChatGPT/monome-emulator/tests/mosaic_audio.py:42), [mosaic_jf.py:44](/mnt/c/Users/andy/Documents/ChatGPT/monome-emulator/tests/mosaic_jf.py:44)). Add reordered notes, globally shifted phrase, wrong duration, and channel-swap fixtures. Separate relative musical timing from absolute input-to-output latency: require an independently bounded clock mapping for the latter, and mark it unverified if unavailable. Crow input acknowledgment precedes detector evaluation and asynchronous callbacks ([crow-capture-api.md:45](/mnt/c/Users/andy/Documents/ChatGPT/monome-emulator/docs/architecture/crow-capture-api.md:45)).

Apply these amendments to both the scope prose and corresponding JSON families; retain their planned status. Emulator history confirms `f301e76` records integration rather than new implementation, consistent with the plan.

**CONFIDENCE: High.** Source/docs/history were inspected read-only; runtime composition, detector tolerances and executable coverage were not verified.
